smoking_gun_arithmetic.interpretation: The observed p50 is almost exactly the sum of one raw PCIe pass and one plausible DRAM gather pass. This strongly implicates the mmap-to-pinned bounce path rather than the PCIe floor itself.

end_to_end_budget.warning: These combine separate synthetic measurements and are not a real full-model result.

page_geometry.hypothesis: One expert per 2 MiB nonpageable allocation reduces the mapping granularity from 237,600 4-KiB pages to 480 large pages per token. GPU/IOMMU benefits must be measured; they are not assumed.

candidate_paths.description: Existing mmap -> 8 pinned windows -> 480 cudaMemcpyAsync operations.
Register stable bank ranges and issue one cudaMemcpyBatchAsync for the ten active expert records of each layer.
ERVG/Q5 kernel directly reads mapped page-locked host records; no HBM staging.
If an architecture probe succeeds, adapt a DAK-style producer/consumer kernel that fetches host Q5 tiles directly into SMEM.
Allocate a 48-GiB, one-expert-per-large-page bank at startup; requires SeLockMemoryPrivilege and probably 96 GiB RAM.

hardware_decision.rule: Buy 96 GiB only if full-bank registration/large-page allocation fails on 64 GiB or if an A/B run shows that removing hard faults substantially reduces p95 after the bounce path is removed.
